scope: Optional SDK adapter logging cannot throw over transaction outcomes or mutate evidence returned to callers. Log context is cloned and synchronous throws/asynchronous rejections are contained.
coverage: Throws while logging start/success preserve one SDK call and successful evidence.
Error-sink failure preserves the original SDK error object.
Logger mutation cannot change returned circuit, identifier or height.
Rejected asynchronous info/error sinks do not create unhandled rejections or change SDK success/failure.
limits: Logger execution is not sandboxed or preempted; a synchronously blocking logger can still block execution.
Logging failures are intentionally discarded; this does not make logs a durable audit journal.
Deployment uses the same protected logging helper, but new cases exercise transitions.
No new browser/full workspace/runtime image/native-wallet validation.
